heading: Purchase of goods without quotation
conditions: Goods not available on GeM or valid GeM Non-Availability Certificate (NAC)
Estimated value up to ₹50,000 on each occasion
Mandatory certificate of quality and reasonable price by the competent buyer
text: Rule 154: Purchase of goods without quotation. Purchase of goods upto the value of ₹50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) on each occasion may be made without inviting quotations or bids on the basis of a certificate to be recorded by the competent authority in the following format: 'I, am personally satisfied that these goods purchased are of the requisite quality and specification and have been purchased from a reliable supplier at a reasonable price.' Provided that goods are not available on GeM or procurement through GeM is not feasible for reasons to be recorded.

heading: Special Financial Threshold under Rule 154 for Scientific Research & Educational Institutions
conditions: Applies strictly to specified scientific ministries, departments, organisations, and educational/research institutes conducting postgraduate or doctoral research
Procurement must be directly for scientific research apparatus, laboratory consumables, or scientific equipment
Threshold is raised up to ₹2,00,000 on each occasion without quotation
Subject to statutory scientific certificate recorded by the researcher/faculty
text: Special Provision to Rule 154: For specified scientific Ministries, Departments, autonomous research organisations, and higher educational and research institutions conducting postgraduate and doctoral research programmes, the threshold for purchase of scientific equipment, chemicals, and laboratory consumables for research without quotation is enhanced upto ₹2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh only) on each occasion, subject to certification by the concerned investigator/competent authority regarding specification, quality, and reasonable price.

heading: Purchase of goods without quotation (GFR 2017 Original)
conditions: Applies to procurements executed between 01-03-2017 and 31-01-2026
Threshold limit: ₹25,000 on each occasion
Officer certificate required
text: Rule 154 (Original GFR 2017): Purchase of goods upto the value of ₹25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) on each occasion may be made without inviting quotations or bids on the basis of a certificate to be recorded by the competent authority in the prescribed format.

heading: Purchase of goods by Purchase Committee
conditions: Goods not available on GeM or procurement on GeM not feasible
Estimated value above ₹50,000 and up to ₹5,00,000 on each occasion
Mandatory three-member Local Purchase Committee constituted by competent authority
Market survey of at least 3 reliable firms to ascertain reasonableness of rate, quality, and specifications
Joint certificate signed by all committee members
text: Rule 155: Purchase of goods by Purchase Committee. Purchase of goods costing above ₹50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) and upto ₹5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lakh only) on each occasion may be made on the recommendations of a duly constituted Local Purchase Committee consisting of three members of an appropriate level as decided by the Head of the Department. The committee will survey the market to ascertain the reasonableness of rate, quality and specifications and identify the appropriate supplier. Before recommending placement of the purchase order, the members will jointly record a certificate: 'We, the members of the purchase committee are jointly and individually satisfied that the goods recommended for purchase are of the requisite specification and quality, have been priced reasonably and the supplier recommended is reliable.'

heading: Special Financial Threshold under Rule 155 for Scientific Research
conditions: Applies to specified scientific ministries, research organisations, and institutes conducting PG/doctoral research
Directly for scientific equipment and research consumables
Threshold value above ₹2,00,000 and up to ₹25,00,000 on each occasion
Constituted Scientific Purchase Committee of 3 domain experts/faculty
Joint satisfaction certificate required
text: Special Provision to Rule 155: For specified scientific research organisations and higher educational institutions, purchase of goods for scientific and research purposes costing above ₹2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh only) and upto ₹25,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakh only) on each occasion may be made on the recommendations of a duly constituted Scientific Purchase Committee of three members, following market survey and joint certification of quality, specifications, and reasonableness of prices.

heading: Purchase of goods by Purchase Committee (GFR 2017 Original)
conditions: Applies to procurements between 01-03-2017 and 31-01-2026
Threshold limit: above ₹25,000 and up to ₹2,50,000
Three-member committee joint certificate
text: Rule 155 (Original GFR 2017): Purchase of goods costing above ₹25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) and upto ₹2,50,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh Fifty Thousand only) on each occasion may be made on the recommendations of a duly constituted Local Purchase Committee consisting of three members of an appropriate level.

heading: Government e-Marketplace (GeM) Mandate and Threshold Bands
conditions: Mandatory procurement of common use Goods and Services available on GeM
Band 1: Up to ₹25,000 through any available supplier on GeM meeting requisite quality, specification and delivery period (Direct Purchase on GeM)
Band 2: Above ₹25,000 and up to ₹5,00,000 through the GeM Seller having the lowest price (L1) amongst available sellers on GeM meeting specifications, comparing at least three different manufacturers
Band 3: Above ₹5,00,000 through the proprietary tool / online bidding or reverse auction on GeM
Procurement outside GeM is strictly impermissible without documented Non-Availability Certificate (NAC) or exemption
text: Rule 149: Government e-Marketplace (GeM). The procurement of common use Goods and Services by Ministries or Departments will be mandatory for Goods or Services available on GeM. The credentials of suppliers on GeM shall be certified by GeM SPV. The procuring authority will determine the reasonableness of rates. The following procedure shall be followed for procurement through GeM: (i) Up to ₹25,000/- through any of the available suppliers on the GeM, meeting the requisite quality, specification and delivery period. (ii) Above ₹25,000/- and up to ₹5,00,000/- through the GeM Seller having lowest price amongst the available sellers on the GeM, of at least three different manufacturers, on GeM, meeting the requisite quality, specification and delivery period. (iii) Above ₹5,00,000/- through the supplier having lowest price with comprehensively comparing the offers, or through online bidding or reverse auction tool provided on GeM.

heading: Limited Tender Enquiry (LTE)
conditions: Applicable for purchase of goods estimated value up to ₹25,00,000
Enquiry sent directly to more than three registered suppliers
Sufficient time allowed for tender submission
Can exceed ₹25 Lakhs only under special emergency/urgency justification certified by CA
text: Rule 161: Limited Tender Enquiry. This method may be adopted when estimated value of the goods to be procured is up to ₹25,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakh only). Copies of the bidding documents should be sent directly to more than three registered suppliers. The number of supplier firms in Limited Tender Enquiry should normally be more than three. Where the demand is urgent and additional expenditure will be involved in advertised tender, or sources of supply are definitely known and limited, LTE may be adopted with reasons placed on record.

heading: Advertised Tender Enquiry / Open Competitive Bidding
conditions: Mandatory for procurement of goods estimated value of ₹25,00,000 and above
Mandatory publication on Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP) and Ministry/Institute website
Standard two-bid system (Technical and Financial) for complex/capital equipment
text: Rule 162: Advertised Tender Enquiry. Subject to exceptions under Rule 161, invitation to tenders by advertisement should be used for procurement of goods of estimated value of ₹25 Lakhs (Rupees Twenty Five Lakh) and above. Advertisement in such cases should be given on the Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP) at www.eprocure.gov.in and on GeM / Ministry / Department's website. Minimum time for submission of bids should be three weeks.

heading: Single Tender Enquiry / Proprietary Article Certificate (PAC)
conditions: Procurement from a single source may be resorted to only in case of: (i) OEM spare parts/compatibility, (ii) Proprietary technology where no alternative exists, (iii) Emergency/national interest
Mandatory PAC Certificate in prescribed statutory format
Requires explicit approval of the designated Competent Authority
Cannot be assumed merely from vendor's claim of sole dealership
text: Rule 166: Single Tender Enquiry. Procurement from a single source may be resorted to in the following circumstances: (i) It is in the knowledge of the user department that only a particular firm is the manufacturer of the required goods. (ii) In a case of emergency, the required goods are necessarily to be purchased from a particular source. (iii) For standardization of machinery or spare parts to be compatible to the existing sets of equipments. Provided that PAC (Proprietary Article Certificate) is signed by the concerned official and approved by the Competent Authority. Sole distributorship or dealer certificate does not make an item proprietary.

heading: Fundamental Principles of Public Procurement and Prohibition of Splitting
conditions: Every authority delegated with financial powers shall observe highest standards of financial integrity and transparency

Demand for goods should not be divided into smaller quantities for making piece-meal purchases to avoid the necessity of obtaining the sanction of higher authority required with reference to the estimated value of the total demand
Purchases across proximate dates for similar items must be aggregated
text: Rule 144: Fundamental principles of public procurement. Every authority delegated with the financial powers of procuring goods in public interest shall have the responsibility and accountability to bring efficiency, economy, and transparency. A demand for goods should not be divided into smaller quantities for making piece meal purchases for avoiding the necessity of obtaining the sanction of higher authority required with reference to the estimated value of the total demand.

heading: Classification of Composite Contracts involving Goods, Installation, and Incidental Services
conditions: Where procurement includes equipment along with installation, commissioning, testing, training, or AMC, the contract is classified primarily as GOODS if the value of physical equipment constitutes the predominant share and services are incidental
If civil works or custom development dominates the contract value, it must be classified under Works or Consultancy Services
AMC exceeding beyond warranty requires explicit service procurement guidelines
text: Para 1.8 Classification of Composite Contracts: Procurement involving physical goods with incidental services such as installation, commissioning, testing, operator training, and post-warranty maintenance (AMC/CMC) shall be treated as Procurement of Goods if the physical equipment forms the predominant purpose and core value of the contract. However, when the installation requires major civil or structural alterations, the civil portion shall follow Works manual procedures.

heading: Classification of Non-Consultancy Services
conditions: Services that have measurable physical outputs or standard repetitive deliverables (e.g. housekeeping, equipment maintenance/AMC, data entry, transport, security, catering, routine IT helpdesk)
Does not require intellectual, conceptual, or policy advice
Procurement follows non-consultancy service bidding frameworks
text: Para 1.3 Non-Consultancy Services: Non-consultancy services involve physical, measurable, routine, or repetitive deliverables where the performance standards can be defined quantitatively. Examples include equipment maintenance contracts (AMC), facilities management, transportation, physical security, courier, catering, and standard IT infrastructure operations.

heading: Procurement of Consultancy Services and Bespoke IT Architecture
conditions: Services of an intellectual, advisory, or analytical nature requiring specialized professional knowledge
Includes bespoke software design, enterprise architecture, custom algorithm development, strategic feasibility studies, and legal/financial advisory
Selection methods include QCBS (Quality and Cost Based Selection), LCS (Least Cost Selection), and SSS (Single Source Selection)
Must not be procured under routine goods direct purchase rules
text: Para 1.4 Consultancy Services: Consultancy services are of an intellectual and advisory nature requiring specialized expert evaluation. It encompasses custom software application development, IT enterprise architecture planning, project management consultancy, strategic advisory, and specialized design. Procurements requiring unique conceptual input must adhere to the consultancy selection framework (QCBS/LCS/FBS).

heading: Definition and Thresholds for Procurement of Works
conditions: Covers construction, fabrication, erection, civil repairs, structural renovation, and electrical substation installations
Works up to ₹10 Lakhs may be executed without quotation or through local quotation under specific institutional work rules; works above ₹10 Lakhs require tender through CPWD / engineering division
Must not be mixed into goods without clear breakdown
text: Para 1.2 Procurement of Works: Works contracts involve civil, mechanical, structural, or electrical engineering construction, structural additions, alterations, and repairs. Procurement of works must be executed through approved engineering departments or recognized public works organizations following CPWD / Departmental Works manuals.

heading: Institutional Purchase Guidelines - Internal Discipline Thresholds
conditions: SYNTHETIC / DEMONSTRATION POLICY: Applies to internal institute procurement at NITR
Direct purchase internal ceiling capped at ₹40,000 to promote committee review
Purchases between ₹40,000 and ₹5,00,000 mandate Departmental Purchase Committee
text: [SYNTHETIC / DEMONSTRATION POLICY] Clause 4.1: Internal Approval Ceilings. Notwithstanding the central GFR upper ceiling, in order to enforce institutional financial prudence, direct purchases by individual department buyers without quotation are capped at ₹40,000 per occasion. Any procurement above ₹40,000 shall be routed through a Departmental Purchase Committee.

heading: Purported Direct Purchase without GeM search up to ₹75,000 [DELIBERATE CONFLICT CLAUSE]
conditions: SYNTHETIC / DEMONSTRATION POLICY: Intentionally conflicting internal clause
Purports to permit HoD to directly buy lab goods up to ₹75,000 without GeM search
Directly violates Central GFR Rule 154 (₹50,000 ceiling) and Rule 149 (mandatory GeM first)
text: [SYNTHETIC / DEMONSTRATION POLICY - DELIBERATE CONFLICT] Clause 4.2: The Head of Department may directly authorize procurement of lab consumables and office articles up to ₹75,000 on cash/single voucher basis without prior GeM portal search, provided vendor delivers within 48 hours.

rule_ref: Institute Manual Schedule B - Delegation Matrix
heading: Delegation of Financial Powers Matrix
conditions: Principal Investigator (PI) has financial authority up to ₹1,00,000 for approved sponsored project funds
Head of Department (HoD) has financial authority up to ₹1,00,000 for recurring departmental budget
Dean (R&C / Academic) has financial authority up to ₹5,00,000 with finance concurrence
Director has full powers exceeding ₹5,00,000 subject to GFR adherence
text: [SYNTHETIC / DEMONSTRATION POLICY] Schedule B - Financial Delegation Matrix: (a) Principal Investigator (PI): Up to ₹1,00,000 per transaction from sanctioned sponsored project grants. (b) Head of Department (HoD): Up to ₹1,00,000 per transaction from department budget. (c) Dean (R&C / Academic Affairs): Above ₹1,00,000 and up to ₹5,00,000 with prior finance concurrence. (d) Director: Above ₹5,00,000 up to statutory institute ceiling.
